local_storage_protection: AsyncStorage holds inventory cache, kiosk registration including the site PIN in plaintext JSON, and the signed-in name. Not Keychain/Keystore. Preview-phase only — production-candidate must move the PIN off AsyncStorage.
transport_security: Notebook sync is MQTT 3.1.1 over WebSocket TLS (wss) to public brokers: broker.emqx.io:8084, broker.hivemq.com:8884, test.mosquitto.org:8081. No certificate pinning. PairDrop is a user-opened https://pairdrop.net tab. Optional extra-API probe is https://megatory-live.delqurolabs.app/api. Google Fonts loaded on web. GitHub Pages https_enforced=true as of 2026-09-19T19:32Z (html_url https://megatory-live.delqurolabs.app/).

telemetry_review: No analytics SDK. Counts travel to public MQTT as AES-GCM ciphertext. Topic id includes a 20-hex PIN digest.
secret_scan: passed - 0 hits; no .env, keys, or credentials committed
dependency_review: Direct deps: expo 52, @e965/xlsx 0.20.3, query-string 7.1.3. No typosquatting on names reviewed.
advisory_scan: not-triaged - npm audit 27 vulnerabilities (15 moderate, 11 high, 1 critical), primarily Expo/RN toolchain. Same class as oi-003. Not a silent clean.
threat_model: Networked kiosk: (1) public MQTT brokers can see ciphertext, hospital code, and PIN digest in the topic — brute-force of 4-digit PINs is feasible if the topic is known; (2) site PIN in AsyncStorage on a shared iPad is recoverable; (3) last-write-wins notebook has no CRDT — two clocks can clobber COUNT; (4) Test Connection talks to /api which is not the notebook; (5) camera permission only for barcodes. Compensating: AES-GCM with PBKDF2 120k, continue-on-this-clock-only fallback, no privileged API keys in the client.
